cards.title: BiSLW: Bi-Spectral Latent Watermarking for Generative Diffusion Models
cards.venue: arXiv preprint; repository labels ECCV 2026, acceptance not independently verified
cards.mechanism: Learned FiLM-conditioned residual encoders duplicate one message across low/high channelwise DCT bands of the final denoised latent before VAE decoding. Separate learned decoders, consistency loss, and output averaging supply redundancy.
cards.threat_and_detector_access: Regeneration and distortions enter training. Extraction observes the query image through a compatible VAE, the spectral mask, and trained decoders; no diffusion inversion is described.
cards.quantitative_endpoint: Table 2: BiSLW bit accuracy 0.96/0.92 at regeneration timesteps 250/500; PSNR 37.40 dB. Table 1 AI-generated 32-bit row: SSIM 0.91, clean bit accuracy 1.00. These are averaged bit endpoints, not exact-message acceptance.
cards.limitations: Training uses 100,000 MIRFLICKR images; learned machinery differs from BCH extraction. Table 3 reports SSIM 0.87 at 64 bits. Tables/text disagree on some CLIC figures; use explicit table rows. No inspected T4/T5 or authentication result establishes our conjunction.
cards.implication_for_candidate: Agent inference: dual latent DCT carriers are occupied prior art. Two distinct BCH messages with conditioned routing differ from repeated-message redundancy, but novelty and survival remain unestablished.
cards.evidence_classification: Mechanism and numbers: direct-evidence. Candidate implication: agent-inference. Stance: supporting carrier feasibility, inconclusive for our gates.

cards.title: DeepFreqMark: End-To-End Learnable Frequency-Domain Watermarking with Spherical Attack Simulation for Latent Diffusion Models
cards.mechanism: Neural message encoding modifies a 32-by-32 frequency patch of the last initial-noise channel, using DCT or Hermitian FFT. Training substitutes Slerp-to-random-noise perturbations for expensive image attacks and inversion.
cards.threat_and_detector_access: Deployment extraction requires DDIM inversion of the query image, frequency cropping, and a learned decoder. Evaluation uses SD1.5 and 100 DiffusionDB prompts; attacks include diffusion purification.
cards.quantitative_endpoint: Table 2, 32 bits, S=0.6: diff_attacker_60 BER is 1.0000% DCT and 0.3750% FFT; clean BER 0.0000% both; average BER 0.4722%/0.3160%. Table 3 lists FFT 256-bit accuracy 99.44%.
cards.limitations: BER does not establish exact-message acceptance or calibrated FPR. Table 3 imports baseline publication metrics. No strict clean PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS gate appears in inspected experiments. Slerp Gaussian-preservation language is author interpretation; equal norm and distribution preservation need conditions, not merely the interpolation formula.
cards.implication_for_candidate: Agent inference: this supports learned spectral capacity, not posterior-VAE recovery of two BCH payloads. Our lightweight read differs materially from initial-noise inversion. Gaussian Slerp training cannot be assumed appropriate for structured posterior latents.
cards.evidence_classification: Mechanism and numbers: direct-evidence. Gaussian guarantee: author-interpretation. Candidate implications: agent-inference. Stance: inconclusive for our gates.

cards.title: Exploring Weaknesses of Generative Image Watermarks against Latent Frequency Masking
cards.venue: arXiv preprint; HTML carries IEEE copyright but venue unverified
cards.mechanism: VAE-encode, replace selected latent FFT coefficients with Gaussian or regenerated-latent frequencies, inverse-transform, and decode. Masks and mixing beta control disruption; the attack avoids gradients.
cards.threat_and_detector_access: Attacker has a compatible public model and verifier queries, not key, clean image, prompt, or verifier internals. Six SD2.1 watermarks use 1,000 prompts per dataset; mask search uses separate 100 images.
cards.quantitative_endpoint: Table I six-method DiffusionDB averages: Gaussian beta=.4 gives TPR@1%FPR .36, PSNR 21.6, SSIM .802, LPIPS .119; diffusion beta=0 gives .44, 28.4, .897, .043. Table II Tree-Ring Gaussian beta=0: TPR .001, PSNR 19.4.
cards.limitations: These quality values do not satisfy our strict clean gate. Gaussian Shading resists partial masks; diffusion replacement can retain MaXsive evidence. Query search and compatible VAE are required. The Lipschitz distortion bound does not guarantee removal.
cards.implication_for_candidate: Agent inference: predictable compact spectral support is an attack surface. Interleaving two messages within one annulus does not create independent protection against masking that annulus. Note this limitation without expanding the authorized T3/T4/T5 gate.
cards.evidence_classification: Mechanism and numbers: direct-evidence. Candidate implication: agent-inference. Stance: contradicting unconditional robustness, inconclusive for measured candidate survival.
